subject: ss-cardiology
title: Aortic Valve Disease: Stenosis and Regurgitation

steps.tx: **Severe aortic stenosis** is defined by peak aortic **jet velocity** at least **4.0** m/s, mean transvalvular gradient at least **40** mmHg, and aortic valve area at most **1.0** cm2 or indexed AVA at most **0.6** cm2/m2. Once severe stenosis becomes symptomatic with angina, syncope, or heart failure, prompt valve replacement is required.
steps.say: Severe aortic stenosis is defined by peak aortic jet velocity of at least 4 point 0 m/s, mean transvalvular gradient of at least 40 mmHg, and aortic valve area of at most 1 point 0 cm2 or indexed AVA of at most 0 point 6 cm2/m2. Once severe stenosis becomes symptomatic with angina, syncope, or heart failure, prompt valve replacement is required.

steps.tx: Classical **low-flow**, low-gradient severe AS with reduced LVEF < **50%**, valve area at most **1.0** cm2, and mean gradient < **40** mmHg requires **dobutamine stress echocardiography** to distinguish true severe AS from pseudo-severe stenosis. In true severe stenosis, stroke volume increases while valve area remains fixed at most 1.0 cm2.
steps.say: Classical low-flow, low-gradient severe AS with reduced LVEF less than 50%, valve area at most 1 point 0 cm2, and mean gradient less than 40 mmHg requires dobutamine stress echocardiography to distinguish true severe AS from pseudo-severe stenosis. In true severe stenosis, stroke volume increases while valve area remains fixed at most 1 point 0 cm2.

nodes.label: Low-Flow Low-Gradient AS (AVA <= 1.0, Mean Grad < 40, EF < 50%)
Low-Dose Dobutamine Stress Echo (Up to 20 mcg/kg/min)
True Severe AS: AVA <= 1.0 & Mean Grad >= 40 mmHg -> Valve Replacement

steps.tx: **Paradoxical low-flow**, low-gradient severe AS occurs with preserved LVEF at least **50%**, valve area at most **1.0** cm2, mean gradient < **40** mmHg, and reduced **stroke volume index** < **35** mL/m2, often seen in elderly hypertensive women with small, concentric hypertrophied left ventricles. Noncontrast CT calcium scoring confirms true stenosis severity.
steps.say: Paradoxical low-flow, low-gradient severe AS occurs with preserved LVEF at least 50%, valve area at most 1 point 0 cm2, mean gradient less than 40 mmHg, and reduced stroke volume index less than 35 mL/m2, often seen in elderly hypertensive women with small, concentric hypertrophied left ventricles. Noncontrast CT calcium scoring confirms true stenosis severity.

right.title: Paradoxical Low-Flow Low-Gradient AS
points: Severe concentric LVH with small ventricular cavity
Stroke volume index < 35 mL/m2 despite normal EF
Evaluated with noncontrast CT aortic valve calcium score

steps.tx: **Transcatheter aortic valve implantation** is preferred over surgical aortic valve replacement in patients aged **75** to **80** years or older or high surgical risk, whereas **SAVR** is favored in younger patients under 65 years. Dedicated Heart Team assessment balances vascular anatomical feasibility against long-term bioprosthetic durability.

steps.tx: **Bicuspid aortic valve** is the most common congenital heart defect affecting **1%** to **2%** of the population, categorized by **Sievers classification** based on the number of raphes into type **0**, type **1**, and type **2**. Type 1 with fusion of the right and left coronary cusps is the most frequent morphological variant.

steps.tx: Severe **chronic aortic regurgitation** is defined by **vena contracta** width > **6** mm, regurgitant volume at least **60** mL/beat, regurgitant fraction at least 50%, or pressure half-time < **200** ms on Doppler echocardiography, with normal resting ejection fraction exceeding **65%**. Severe regurgitation produces marked progressive left ventricular volume overload.
steps.say: Severe chronic aortic regurgitation is defined by vena contracta width greater than 6 mm, regurgitant volume at least 60 mL/beat, regurgitant fraction at least 50%, or pressure half-time less than 200 ms on Doppler echocardiography, with normal resting ejection fraction exceeding 65%. Severe regurgitation produces marked progressive left ventricular volume overload.

steps.tx: Surgical aortic valve replacement is indicated for **asymptomatic severe aortic regurgitation** when resting left ventricular ejection fraction is at most **50%**, or **LV end-systolic dimension** exceeds **50** mm or **25** mm/m2. Intervening prior to irreversible myocardial fibrosis preserves long-term postoperative systolic function.

steps.tx: Peripheral signs of severe chronic aortic regurgitation include the **Corrigan water-hammer pulse** with bounding carotid upstroke and rapid collapse, and the **Quincke pulse** showing capillary pulsations in the nail bed. These classic physical manifestations reflect a widened pulse pressure driven by rapid diastolic runoff into the left ventricle.
